name: BSP_InputDeviceTable_ResetSlots
evidence: Hypothesis, not a recovered symbol; the verb comes from the call site, not from the callee. Packet app_init_input, Ghidra read-only. __fastcall on ECX, RET with no operand, no stack arguments. Walks this+0x04 as Device*[3][8] in class-major order and invokes vtable slot index 5 (offset +0x14) with ECX only and no arguments on every non-null entry. Rows are keyboard, mouse and joystick/gamepad, proved by the guards at this+0x04 and this+0x24 and the joystick store at this+0x44+i*4 in 00a98030. The base device implements +0x14 as a bare RET at 00a93e80, so the semantics live in an override this packet did not locate. The 3-byte Ghidra gap at 00a900fd is alignment padding. Evidence: docs/APP_INIT_INPUT.md; reports/app_init_input.json.

name: BSP_InputDeviceTable_AnyJoystickButtonDown
evidence: Hypothesis, not a recovered symbol. Packet game_blocking_screen_frame, read-only analysis. Provisional. __fastcall, ECX = the input device table DAT_00f8bbf4, no arguments, returns AL. Walks the eight pointers at this+0x44..this+0x60, which docs/APP_INIT_INPUT.md establishes as the joystick row of the 3x8 slot array (row base this+0x04 + class*0x20), skips nulls and returns 1 as soon as one device's virtual +0x2c returns non-zero, else 0. Device virtual +0x2c is 00a93f60, which polls indices 0..0x3b through virtual +0x20, so the query means 'any button on any joystick is down'. Sole caller BSP_Game_UpdateBlockingScreen.

name: BSP_InputDeviceTable_AttachDevice
evidence: Hypothesis, not a recovered symbol. Packet app_init_input, Ghidra read-only. __thiscall, two stack arguments, RET 8. Reads the device class from vtable+0x08 (0..2), resolves a requested slot of 0xffffffff to the first free column of that class row by scanning this+4+class*0x20 for eight entries, stores the resolved column into the device at +0x08, then writes the pointer to this+4+(slot+class*8)*4. This scan is what pins the array to Device*[3][8]. A full row leaves the counter at 8 and the store lands outside the row. Callers 00a982d0 and 00a98030. Evidence: docs/APP_INIT_INPUT.md; reports/app_init_input.json.

name: BSP_InputDeviceTable_AnyDynamicDeviceButtonDown
evidence: Hypothesis, not a recovered symbol. Packet game_blocking_screen_frame, read-only analysis. Provisional. __fastcall, ECX = the input device table DAT_00f8bbf4, no arguments, returns AL. Walks the checked vector whose proxy is at this+0x6c (_Myfirst +0x70, _Mylast +0x74), skips nulls and returns 1 as soon as one element's virtual +0x2c returns non-zero, else 0; the interleaved CALLs to 00bf6713 are _SECURE_SCL iterator assertions. Same virtual +0x2c (00a93f60, buttons 0..0x3b) as BSP_InputDeviceTable_AnyJoystickButtonDown, so the pair together answer 'is any button down on any device'. Four callers: 004b43b0, 004db920, 00532c50 and BSP_Game_UpdateBlockingScreen.

name: BSP_InputAction_ForceHeld
evidence: Hypothesis, not a recovered symbol. Packet game_frame_input_tick, read-only analysis. __thiscall(this = 30h action record, float amount), RET 4. Sets both down latches (+20h and +28h) and writes amount into both hold times (+1Ch and +24h). Because the previous half is left down, 004c43c0 reports no edge; this is the continue case of the timed action set at game+5BCh (004e4fba), used on every visit after the first. Sole caller BSP_Game_OnMove.

name: BSP_InputAction_UpdateListenerState
evidence: Provisional. Hypothesis, not a recovered symbol. Packet game_frame_input_tick, read-only analysis. __thiscall(this = listener at action record+2Ch, float seconds, int previous_down, int current_down), RET 0Ch; both booleans are 'latch != 0 && hold > 0.0f' applied to the record's previous pair (+20h/+1Ch) and current pair (+28h/+24h) at 00a92ca6..00a92ce0. Accumulates seconds into the floats at +14h, +18h, +1Ch and +20h, zeroing +18h on the press branch (00a91b09) and +14h on the release branch (00a91b86), and derives twelve flag bytes at +8h..+13h against the thresholds 00e12f20 (press/release/hold gate), 00e12f24 (repeat) and 00e12f28 (subtracted from +20h on a repeat, 00a91b27). Tail derives +09h = +08h && +0Ah and +0Ch = +0Bh && +0Dh. Named flags come from 00a926f0: +0Bh is fastRelease, +10h is holdPress. The branch structure juggles three live x87 values and was not fully recovered. Sole caller 00a92c40. | Provisional. Hypothesis, not a recovered symbol. Correction superseding the earlier game_frame_input_tick partial analysis: docs/INPUT_ACTION_CLASSIFIER.md recovers all branches from the x87 listing. Native ECX=listener, stack float delta then low-byte previous/current state, RET 0Ch. Binary32 clocks +14h and +18h mean time since release and since press respectively. +09h is +08h AND NOT +0Ah, and +0Ch is +0Bh AND NOT +0Dh (JNZ at 00a91b97/00a91baa). Ordered strict quick-edge/expiry/repeat comparisons and inclusive held threshold use image defaults 0.25f/0.5f/0.1f. Only one repeat subtraction per continuing-down call. Current callers 00a92a20, 00a92c40, 00a92d40. Reconstructed explicit-state C++ passed Win32 build and 25088 local native differential state comparisons; NaN payloads/FPU exceptions and game behavior are not established. No native ABI compatibility claim.

name: BSP_InputAction_Reset
evidence: Hypothesis, not a recovered symbol. Packet game_frame_input_tick, read-only analysis. __thiscall(this = 30h action record), RET, no stack arguments. Zeroes the record's previous/current pair (+1Ch, +20h, +24h, +28h) and, when the listener pointer at +2Ch is non-null, clears the listener's twelve flag bytes at +8h..+13h and its four float accumulators at +14h, +18h, +1Ch and +20h (00a91e46..00a91e79). Called once per node of the std::set<int> at game+5B0h from BSP_Game_OnMove 004e4ec2, so that set is the per-frame action suppression list.

name: BSP_InputAction_RebindDeviceReferences
evidence: Provisional. Hypothesis, not a recovered symbol. docs/INPUT_ACTION_CLASSIFIER.md. ECX=30h action record, no stack arguments, RET. Walk +10h/count+14h with 34h binding stride; clear valid byte, skip primary class -1 without clearing cached pointer, resolve device from backend 00f8bbf4 +6Ch+class*24h vector (begin+4/end+8), write cache +0Ch, then sequentially resolve required (binding+18h/count+1Ch) and forbidden (+24h/count+28h) 14h modifier arrays whose cached device is +8. Stop each binding at first missing pointer, preserving later caches; mark valid only after both arrays finish. Unsigned device index bounds checked; class validity and stable valid vectors are preconditions. Redundant library bounds diagnostics remain external and unreachable under that contract. Reconstructed and Win32 build-tested, not native-differential or game-validated.

name: BSP_InputManager_RebindAllActions
evidence: Hypothesis, not a recovered symbol. Packet game_frame_input_tick, read-only analysis. __thiscall(this = input singleton), RET. Walks the action table (base singleton+4h, count singleton+8h, stride 30h) calling 00a91e80 on every record, which re-resolves that record's 34h-stride binding array at +10h/+14h. Reached from 00a92c40 only when the device backend byte 00f8bbf4+D4h was set, which 00a92c66 clears, so this is the device-change rebind.

name: BSP_InputAction_PollBindings
evidence: Hypothesis, not a recovered symbol. Packet game_frame_input_tick, read-only analysis. __thiscall(this = 30h action record), RET. Prologue 00a9237a..00a9238c copies the current hold time at +24h into +1Ch and the current down latch at +28h into +20h, then zeroes +24h/+28h; this shift is what makes the reviewed 004c43c0 test a rising edge. The body then walks the record's 34h-stride binding array from +10h with the count at +14h, probing device vtable+20h and reading analogue values through vtable+24h. Sole caller 00a92c40.

name: BSP_InputAction_ApplyModifierName
evidence: Hypothesis, not a recovered symbol. Packet game_frame_input_tick, read-only analysis. __thiscall(this = action listener, void* param), RET 4. Reads the C string at param+4h; when it is non-null and equals 'fastRelease' (00d5b624) under __stricmp 00bf7fbf it sets listener byte +0Bh and returns. Otherwise it queries the parameter block itself about 'holdPress' (00d5b618) through the method at 00425850 and sets listener byte +10h when that returns true. These are the only two named bits of the twelve-flag listener block; sole caller 00a92aa0.

name: BSP_InputAction_ForcePressed
evidence: Hypothesis, not a recovered symbol. Packet game_frame_input_tick, read-only analysis. __thiscall(this = 30h action record, float amount, void* param), RET 8. Clears the previous half (+1Ch = 0, +20h = 0), sets the current half down (+28h = 1, +24h = amount) and, when the first dword of param is non-zero, calls 00a926f0 with ECX = the listener at record+2Ch. The cleared previous half is exactly what makes 004c43c0 report a rising edge, so this is the start case of the timed action set at game+5BCh (004e4f98), latched by the node byte at +20h. Sole caller BSP_Game_OnMove.

name: BSP_InputManager_Update
evidence: Hypothesis, not a recovered symbol. Packet game_on_move_map, read-only analysis. __thiscall(this, float delta); ECX is the 004bec00 input singleton (mov ecx,eax at 004e4a6d). Forwards the delta to backend DAT_00f8bbf4 vtable+4, then walks 0x30-byte action records with float hold timers at +0x1C/+0x24 and latch bytes at +0x20/+0x28. First simulation call of every frame. | Packet game_frame_input_tick: full body recovered from the listing. Order is backend 00f8bbf4 vtable+4h with the delta (00a92c57), read-and-clear the rebind byte 00f8bbf4+D4h then 00a922a0 when it was set (00a92c5e..00a92c71), then per record with +01h set: 00a92370, and when the listener at +2Ch is non-null 00a91a50 with (delta, previous_down, current_down) where both booleans are 'latch != 0 && hold > 0.0f' over +20h/+1Ch and +28h/+24h; finally the optional plain function pointer at 00f8bbfc (00a92d0d). The +2Ch null test is obfuscated as neg/sbb/test 0F8BC00h at 00a92c9a. Base and count are reloaded from singleton+4h/+8h each iteration, and +8h is a count (end = base + count*30h), not an end pointer. Reconstructed in src/input_tick.cpp; see docs/GAME_INPUT_TICK.md.

name: BSP_InputDeviceManager_OnDeviceEnumerated
evidence: Hypothesis, not a recovered symbol. Packet app_init_input, Ghidra read-only. Body of the DIEnumDevicesCallbackA thunk at 00a982b0 (three instructions, RET 8, always DIENUM_CONTINUE). Switches on the low byte of lpddi->dwDevType at +0x24 and reads tszProductName at +0x12c, so DIDEVICEINSTANCEA is in use. DI8DEVTYPE_KEYBOARD 0x13 allocates 0x310 and constructs 00a9a3e0 into class 0 slot 0, guarded by this+0x04; DI8DEVTYPE_MOUSE 0x12 allocates 0x23c and constructs 00a9a290 into class 1 slot 0, guarded by this+0x24; DI8DEVTYPE_JOYSTICK 0x14 and DI8DEVTYPE_GAMEPAD 0x15 allocate 0xb48 and construct 00a99940 into class 2 at the first free column, skipping instance GUIDs already in the 16-byte-stride vector at this+0xe8. Sets this+0xf4 when the product name matches Xbox/XBOX/XBox and 360. Evidence: docs/APP_INIT_INPUT.md; reports/app_init_input.json.

name: BSP_InputDeviceManager_Construct
evidence: Hypothesis, not a recovered symbol. Packet app_init_input, Ghidra read-only; supersedes the earlier BSP_DirectInput_CreateDevices, which understated it as a factory. __fastcall on ECX, RET with no operand, returns this in EAX, so it is a constructor. Calls the base helper 00a91570, stamps vtable 00d5b72c, zeroes +0xe0/+0xe8/+0xec/+0xf0/+0xf4, then DirectInput8Create(GetModuleHandleA(nullptr), 0x0800, IID_IDirectInput8A at 00d78d8c, &this+0xe0, nullptr), AddRef through vtable+0x04 and EnumDevices(DI8DEVCLASS_ALL, callback 00a982b0, this, DIEDFL_ATTACHEDONLY) through vtable+0x10. It then allocates four 0x240-byte devices, constructs each with 00a9a5a0(index) and attaches them with 00a904e0(this, -1, device). The HRESULT is discarded and the pointer dereferenced on the next instruction; a failed allocation is passed on as null. Evidence: docs/APP_INIT_INPUT.md; reports/app_init_input.json.

name: BSP_GuiListControl_SetItemVisible
evidence: Hypothesis, not a recovered symbol. __thiscall(control, int index, char visible), RET 8. Walks the item list at +FCh..+100h counting to index, then stores 0 into the item widget's +77h when the third argument is set (00A9C3D2) and 1 when it is clear (00A9C3E7). This is what establishes widget+77h as hidden rather than visible; it is the only writer of the byte outside the two constructors. Evidence in docs/GUI_WIDGET_SCENE_VISIBILITY.md.

name: BSP_GuiListControl_SetVisible
evidence: Hypothesis, not a recovered symbol. __thiscall(widget, char visible), RET 4, widget vtable +34h in table 00d5bbf8. No Ghidra function: raw listing 00A9CCE0-00A9CD16. Calls the base 00AA8530 and then, when the id at +118h is not -1, resolves it through BSP_GuiManager_GetOrCreate (004C12B0) and 00AA0F50 and calls the same virtual +34h on the result, so one widget can slave another's visibility. Evidence in docs/GUI_WIDGET_SCENE_VISIBILITY.md.

name: BSP_GuiListControl_SetActive
evidence: Hypothesis, not a recovered symbol. __thiscall(widget, char active), RET 4, widget vtable +60h in table 00d5bbf8. 00A9CD2C calls the base 00AA6A30 with ECX still holding this, which Ghidra drops. When the byte is being cleared and byte +11Eh is set, 00A9CD50 to 00A9CDA9 walks the item list at +FCh..+10Ch calling 00A9BA90(&list, node, node != [this+10Ch] ? 3 : 1), so the selected entry gets state 1 and the rest state 3. Evidence in docs/GUI_WIDGET_SCENE_VISIBILITY.md.

name: BSP_GuiWidget_IsKindOf

name: BSP_GuiWidget_SetPivot

name: BSP_GuiWidget_IsVisible
evidence: Hypothesis, not a recovered symbol. __thiscall(widget) -> bool in EAX, RET, no arguments. No Ghidra function: raw listing 00A9E0D0-00A9E0F0. Returns false when the node at +4Ch is null, otherwise compares the node's visibility factor at +ACh against the float 0.0 at 00d7a218 with COMISS and JBE, so a NaN factor is not visible. name: BSP_GuiWidget_GetTypeId
evidence: Hypothesis, not a recovered symbol. __thiscall(widget), RET, two instructions MOV EAX,[ECX+60h]; RET at 00a9e110..00a9e113. Base vtable 00d5bbf8 slot +5Ch. Widget+60h is the type tag the base constructor 00AA9390 takes as its only argument (0Bh for the 00A9DF40 class, 6 for the 00AB5C60 class). Ghidra has no function at this address: the body is raw listing followed by int3 padding, so it must be defined before the name can be applied. docs/GUI_WIDGET_TRANSFORM.md.

name: BSP_Localization_ResolveKey
evidence: Hypothesis, not a recovered symbol. Provisional, analysis only. Single-key resolver: strips an optional leading "^", treats a leading "." as a marker that suppresses the map lookup, then looks the remainder up with 00a9ec70 and falls back to the wide string built from 00f8bc54. The resolved text is then scanned for the "#" marker at 00cf828c and substituted in a loop. Neither the substitution semantics nor the "^" meaning were established. Evidence: docs/APP_INIT_LOCALE.md; reports/app_init_locale.json.

name: BSP_Localization_ResolveKeyList
evidence: Hypothesis, not a recovered symbol. Splits the lookup key on the delimiter set "|" with _strcspn and calls 00a9f4b0 for each piece, appending into the caller wide string. Eleven callers across GUI, text and network code, all reached from the manager singleton 00f8bc4c. Provisional: only the split was reconstructed. Evidence: docs/APP_INIT_LOCALE.md; reports/app_init_locale.json.

name: BSP_StringMap_InsertOrGet
evidence: Hypothesis, not a recovered symbol. __thiscall, ECX = the bucket array, one native-string key pointer, returns the value slot at node+8. Hash folds only A-Z with the (byte)(c+0xbf)<0x1a test and accumulates h = h*0x83 + (signed char)c, masked with 0xfff over 0x1000 buckets. Walks the chain comparing length then __stricmp and returns the existing node, otherwise increments the count at +0x4000 and pushes a new 0x1c-byte node at the head (prev +0x10, next +0x14, pool index +0x18). Evidence: docs/APP_INIT_LOCALE.md; reports/app_init_locale.json.
